notes.title: 🎉 Free soundtrack for all owners! 🎉 5th year anniversary retrospective & FAQ!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/cac6d81ba692fa41e63fd9999b84bd5b4b6e153b.png[/img]

[h1]The Spy Who Shrunk Me turns five! 🎉[/h1]

It's been a long time since we've piped up here, but here's the good stuff: you're getting an all new, Steam-improved soundtrack directly to your Steam library - to celebrate the 5th anniversary of The Spy Who Shrunk Me.

Read on to also get a sweet retrospective that may answer your questions like, is there gonna be a sequel, what happened to Catland and why is that one bug still not fixed. Trust me, it's a goodie.

[h2]The Soundtrack[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/a6704a9d8ae376b3d7ff09ab65fd816bf4273095.png[/img]

The original soundtrack composed by Oskar Nieminen features nearly an hour of epic spytastic theme tunes, pulse-pounding combat music and that really catchy tune we used for the mandatory vehicle section. All 21 tracks are available through Steam's neat soundtrack system - so it'll appear in your Steam library under "Soundtracks". It's free - as a thank you for playing the game!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/913240/The_Spy_Who_Shrunk_Me__Original_Soundtrack/

[h2]Looking back at The Spy Who Shrunk Me: A Brief Retrospective[/h2]

As most of you know, Catland is long dead. The game IPs were bought out by the CEO & creative director Tomi Toikka (me, the one typing this post) in order to preserve them even after being lost during all the winding-down-a-company hustle. I really think Taphouse VR and The Spy Who Shrunk Me deserve to be enjoyed by gamers long after the company is gone - so I've been preserving, discounting and nurturing them since we wound down operations.

Let me take you back on a history lesson.

[h3]The birth of Catland[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/9c4cb4ecf1e68f920e428bc9f21e58ef55cc31bb.jpg[/img]

We made Catland during a business incubator called Nordic VR Startups (after branded as Nordic XR Startups), and we released our first title, Taphouse VR (which celebrates 6 years, check out the announcement post below - also soundtrack as a gift) in just four months. We started with just 3 devs.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/591680/Taphouse_VR/

Virtual reality was still in its infancy, and we wanted to do a game that really took into account the power of virtual reality. So of course we thought about unique VR stuff - the sense of scale, the feeling of being-there, and changing the scale of the world. 

[h3]Project Spygame is started[/h3]

I got the idea to combine a sort of Austin Powers vibe to an oldie-but-goldie long lost game series called No One Lives Forever combined with the player having a shrink ray, and the idea for our next game The Spy Who Shrunk Me was born.

Here's a really antique YouTube video to show the first prototype state of the game in all its asset-flipped glory.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mneLu0g8BiQ

This is how we pitched the game to the incubator, investors and everybody. It was pretty neat. Yes, I have extremely shaky hands.

So what wound up happening was we got a funding round for the company from a big Finnish venture capital company! I hired the best people I knew to pull it off (about eight people at max capacity, if I recall), but frankly, the game idea was too ambitious for anyone of us and we really bit more than we could chew.

[h3]Shipping fast doesn't mean shipping good[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/dc8c7d596dd916cef3f18bc716c88aaa522691d1.png[/img]

The problems started to arise with the ambitious release plan; we started pitching this November 2017 and wanted to release it the following year. The final release date wound up being December 18, 2018. Then; VR started losing steam (heh) when customers weren't really into all the VR stuff as they used to in, say, back in 2016. 

So we had to pivot the game to both PC and VR just to get a sizable enough audience to get the game going. We had no idea what we were doing - for Unity, we were using an asset pack called UFPS at first but ditched it once we realized it wasn't as expandable as we wanted. So, boatloads of technical debt, never shipped and FPS game before, never done enemy AI before...you could see where we were going.

[h3]A disasterpiece[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/ec7beab45493f475454828b359316b81c2c666e7.png[/img]

It got pretty ugly at times, and I must admit I wasn't at my best. What ended up shipping was a rough estimate of what we really wanted to ship. We rightfully got roasted for lackluster AI, poor controls, bugs, general jankiness and inconsistent gameplay (the bananas and airbag mines were literally the same thing). We even had to ship the VR part of the game after launch, which was not what we promised.

One of the most horrible things that happened was that one popular streamer tried to play the game on launch day - but we had a crash bug which happened if you had a controller connected(!!) when booting up the game! 

[h3]Silver linings[/h3]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ne7-dbYjSEE

What I was immensely proud of was the storyline and humor, which I think we nailed - there were some cringy stuff we had to cut at the end, but the final version of the game at least has a fun spy story with some edge to it! The levels were also nice and varied, even though we could have used a few more different enemy types and more innovative use of the shrink ray. And the speed which we shipped this with, doing the entire game project basically from start to inevitable finish in just 8 months.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/9223b44a617bf75cf7b7e4710adc32dd9c21adbf.png[/img]

Many things can be said about The Spy Who Shrunk Me. The fact it got the reception it did really humbled us. It was too ambitious, too big of a scope and definitely a bit rushed out of the door. If you enjoyed the experience despite all the jank, you got to see what we did best - games that made you think "what the hell are we playing right now". 

I've since tried to keep the game nice and discounted so it at least won't break your bank. I really hope you enjoyed your time with it.

[h3]Five years later[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/803db09a9537f23c3e345f3ac7cd73c634a8d76d.png[/img]

We took the death of Catland pretty hard, but all of us stuck to the gaming industry. I started a new company called [b][url=https://makea.games]Makea Games[/url][/b], of which I'm the CEO, Founder & Creative Director of. For The Spy Who Shrunk Me, I did marketing art, the entire UI, wrote and scripted the cutscenes and story, made the initial prototype and came up with all the gameplay features.

Arttu, the level designer, went on to work for [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/10tons]10tons[/url][/b], another Tampere-based game company (of Crimsonland fame), as a lead level designer for their open-world game Dysmantle.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/846770/DYSMANTLE/

Anssi, one of the founders and programmers, went to work on games like Surviving the Aftermath from [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/iceflake]Iceflake Studios[/url][/b] and other projects, and is now founding a new game company!

Tommi, the other founder and programmer, went onto [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/iceflake]Iceflake Studios[/url][/b] as well to work on Surviving the Aftermath and other cool titles.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/684450/Surviving_the_Aftermath/

Mikko, the programmer working on the VR version, went onto work at [b][url=https://cosmiclounge.com/]Cosmic Lounge[/url][/b].

Many of the rest of the development team moved onto my next venture. Out of the team, Ville (programmer at Catland, now CTO at Makea Games), Bea (environment artist at Catland, now founder at Makea Games) and Pyry (voice actor for all the guards, now game designer at Makea Games) joined me at Makea Games.

If you're interested in what we're working on - we are making the ultimate parkour party game called [b]Supermoves[/b]! You can check out some of the revealed stuff at [b][url=https://supermovesgame.com]supermovesgame.com[/url][/b]. Put it this way; if you like Tony Hawk's, Mirror's Edge, Fall Guys and Minecraft - boy do we have a game for you.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1959580/Supermoves/

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/a2497e68d249539e128574c77a30627e20962894.gif[/img]

[h2]Frequently Asked Questions[/h2]

[b]Is there going to be a sequel/prequel/any followup for The Spy Who Shrunk Me?[/b]
[quote=]Nope, never. We never really made a buck on the game, and while ambitious, we really couldn't make the concept work as we wanted. Better it serve as a shrine for future games of the same type - maybe one day some other team can tackle a NOLF-like stealth game![/quote]

[b]Are you ever going to update or bugfix The Spy Who Shrunk Me?[/b]
[quote=]I'm way too busy with my new company to do that, unfortunately. The game also didn't make enough money to justify any kind of remaster or remake. I'll keep it as-is, as a rough cut, an unpolished gem. I'm also not a programmer, so I can't really go around fixing stuff.[/quote]

[b]Could you release the source code for The Spy Who Shrunk Me?[/b]
[quote=]While technically I have the rights, the game uses a lot of proprietary Unity assets (i.e. the office level props, AURA volumetric lighting, etc.) that have a copyright on them. I'm not legally allowed to distribute the contents of the source archive, even though I have it in my possession, due to the use of these proprietary assets.[/quote]

[b]Will The Spy Who Shrunk Me stay on Steam?[/b]
[quote=]Yes, as long as I am able to host it somewhere. I've been using my friend's company Adjective Animal for the games - the sales go directly to funding the upkeep of stuff like accounting and business costs. I might make my own holding company someday to host it, it's no biggie.

Check out Adjective Animal's games (like the Smash-like topdown hockey game Puck Buddies) [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/adjectiveanimal]here[/url].

[/quote]

[b]Is there an archive of the cutscenes of the game?[/b]
[quote=]Yes! They are properly captioned and everything on YouTube, here:
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oNtmBnzYjSw&list=PLcDyWgxSKzuv2o-qsDdYhe1wtTyyMrRkr]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oNtmBnzYjSw&list=PLcDyWgxSKzuv2o-qsDdYhe1wtTyyMrRkr[/url]
[/quote]

[b]What's up with that one ending where the town of Forssa, Finland gets nuked?[/b]
[quote=]I really, really hated the town of Forssa and everyone in it. I lived there for about seven years - seven was too many. Maybe it has changed in the past few years, I don't know, but I wanted to make fun of it in every Catland game. All the taverns in Taphouse VR are based on actual bars in that town, by the way. It was a good in-joke, I hope someone gets it. Our programmer Anssi wanted to add that "Forssa is a magical place."[/quote]

[b]Can I use the music in the soundtrack in my videos or streaming content?[/b]
[quote=]By all means! Please credit the composer Oskar Nieminen.[/quote]

[b]Whatever happened to Starship Saboteur?[/b]
[quote=]It didn't get funded. It was a neat concept though and I really learned a lot from it.[/quote]

[b]Will Catland ever make a return?[/b]
[quote=]It was my first company and will always be in my heart. That logo I made in 3 minutes (and which required 3 hours to have the eye blink using CSS) is still the best damn logo I ever made. Maybe I'll keep hiding the logo around in my future endeavors to keep the spirit of Catland alive. But no, as a company and a studio, we've all drifted apart to our own ventures - we do keep a DIscord server up for catching up from time to time :) We used to have a saying; "from this poker table, we leave as friends". I hope people remember Catland fondly and give it the love it deserves. That's what we all want. Avenge us! ːsporobarː[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/bf59a846031997df39545e27be776d9795681c5c.png[/img]

[h1]What's next?[/h1]
I'll keep the games nice and tidy in the Steam store so people can play them. Feel free to keep on playing The Spy Who Shrunk Me, grab a copy for your friends. I will keep doing discounts and general maintenance. If you really enjoyed the game and want more from the developers, I'll have some news about my next game soon as a separate announcement.

I can't really say how thankful for I am for all the players who've enjoyed The Spy Who Shrunk Me all these years. Thank you so much for having fun with the game! I wish all the best to you.

Tomi Toikka
Former CEO
Catland

notes.title: Introducing Starship Saboteur: a new game prototype from Catland
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/5ce96ca091a5930b10774bb2863d56104ff225e5.png[/img]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=awqSrYE2HOc

[h1]Download the prototype for free from here:[/h1] [url=https://catland.itch.io/starshipsaboteur]https://catland.itch.io/starshipsaboteur[/url]

[b]In Starship Saboteur, you and your crew must stop a galaxy-wide war by destroying the spaceships that allow it.[/b] Caught in the middle of a tense stalemate between three factions, you and your friends are left for dead in the cold vacuum of space. Vowing revenge, you use your skills of subterfuge and sabotage to stop the war on its tracks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/a33f4016c3c624f37f20a6b420d8ba2dbe76571a.png[/img]
[h1]Sabotage enemy equipment to cause carnage[/h1]
Break everything. Shoot windows out to depressurize entire sections of the ship, turn off the lights to help with stealth, disable to shields to allow an enemy faction to board. Reinforcements being a hassle? Scramble the teleporters, and enemies that spawn in are horrifying fused monsters that pose no threat. Steal the enemies weapons and technology by raiding the Armory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/822c0f61336f2a2f24e03344eb0a7321c18de2e8.png[/img]
[h1]Slaughter everyone on board or go full pacifist, your choice[/h1]
Play your way by completing your objectives with stealth, takedowns, tranquilizer guns and by passing through ventilation shafts. Hide bodies from enemy sight in containers or use them to get past enemy patrols. Go fully invisible with the Stealth Field, use White Noise Grenades to cover your escape and drag the captain into the escape pods to demoralize the entire ship's crew.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eUgAOFT5fzQ

Or go guns blazing with lethal force, utilizing the bullet-bouncing Ricochet Shotgun, infinitely charging Technocrat Plasma Rifle, dual SMGs and room clearing Black Hole Grenades. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/a953e5dbae603673e63cf3cac21c18c36df21c79.png[/img]
[h1]A campaign of choices and consequences[/h1]
In the final game we have a very intricate campaign system where you always have to pick between which of the three factions to attack, enabling great replayability and making sure each campaign you go through is unique. To get the full experience, you are encouraged to complete the campaign multiple times to see all possible gadgets, weapons, playstyles, endings and starships. You can eliminate an entire faction out of the war by sabotaging them enough.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/9d67745c3c3c00f7db990f90c809eb81579228a6.png[/img]
[h1]A small prototype free for you to enjoy[/h1]
As part of our shift to PC and consoles, we have completed a prototype for the game which features one mission and one faction, the Celestial Command's starship Magellan. Ten weapons, six gadgets, multiple enemy types and all playstyles supported with two distinct loadouts (and more weapons that can be picked up from raiding the Armory or taking out enemies).

We are releasing the prototype completely free for you to play and decide if this is something we should make. If we get enough traction, we will look into making this a full game. In-game in the prototype you will find a survey, please fill this out to give us vital information.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/f5f7835ac3a9876c2a1bf65b8be5d09c1d01e033.png[/img]

[h1]Download the prototype here:[/h1]
https://catland.itch.io/starshipsaboteur

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33423885/4dfdc58eec6cc29450d9a67d6ba5f234b0279d7d.png[/img]
[h1]Winds of change for Catland[/h1]
We are no longer making virtual reality games. I know this comes as a bummer to some, but it is a necessary change due to the shifting landscape. Read more about the future of Catland here: [url=https://catland.studio/blog/schrodingers-catland/]https://catland.studio/blog/schrodingers-catland/[/url]

All aboard to new horizons,
Tomi Toikka
CEO
Catland

Main feature of this patch is the VR version of Quaternion Identity

notes.title: The Spy Who Shrunk Me comes out December 18th 2018 for PC & Q1 2019 for VR!
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/d1d6ee50c1e60ebe7d0390f1abd7f8f846522349.png[/img]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/754850/The_Spy_Who_Shrunk_Me/

[h1][b]The Spy Who Shrunk Me launches on PC on December 18th 2018![/b][/h1]

We are launching on Steam Early Access and we'll stay in Early Access until our VR edition is ready for prime time. The game in Early access is playable from start to finish with many exciting missions where you get to save the world before the Cold War turns red hot!

We'll use Early Access to add even more gadgets to the game while cooking up our VR edition. Buying the game in Early Access means you'll be able to get your voice heard and help us refine our stealth experience. So the game's PC version is more-or-less finished, we just want to get out of Early Access with both PC & VR.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/029ae327356414c0daf244b4da136c6ec0b07a52.png[/img]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/bbbff954d5eb0b94b42c842cedcda3142b3da455.gif[/img]

The Spy Who Shrunk Me is a fully voice acted narrative experience where you get to drive a miniature car, drop people down paper shredders and defuse a nuclear missile from within! The game stars the talented [b]Louise Saint-Claire[/b] as Miss Audrey Smoothspy.

Fans of the old classic No One Lives Forever games can rejoice - this game is a huge love letter to the legendary spy game series! We're bringing non-lethality to the classic formula, as we think a smooth spy never should resort to getting caught. If you do get an alarm, you can always hide using your trusty Shrink Ray.

The game is all about [b]pure stealth[/b]. In fact, you can play the entire game through without harming a single soul and never getting detected. A full ghost/pacifist run is possible and even encouraged!

Fancy yourself a bit of a lunatic? You can always just toss every enemy you see into the nearest paper shredder or skip objectives at your leisure. We're not judging. Your employers might.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/64b05f591a7f6f6c06214d08f7a651dbe1d6019f.png[/img]

Missions range from hacking servers, sabotaging equipment, extracting targets and taking out key personnel to saving the world itself from the Soviet menace!

We've got plenty of exciting levels with fun gameplay with narrative twists and turns. As you move further into the CON-NEX complex, you'll figure out secrets of the Soviet Union and ruin the plans of General Boris B. Bolscotchkovich and Ernst E. Eierkopf!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/6ea1454046a57018539460de2720fcc40207e032.png[/img]

After each mission you'll get a handy Mission Report which will give you a SpyScore™ ranking your spy exploits. You can complete objectives in the manner you see fit - even skipping objectives altogether. There are multiple outcomes to specific missions - you'll know it when you see it!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/1bd01b9de8abda97ffd333ecd6faacca3ae22a5e.png[/img]

[h1][b]THE SHRINK RAY[/b][/h1]

You'll get the titular Shrink Ray during your first mission, onboard the Moscow Express!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/6932cafd4c20f5255c9ba537052a0b3b064a853c.gif[/img]

Use your trusty Shrink Ray to squeeze under small spaces and avoid enemy detection. Use your tiny form to easily avoid enemy gunfire and mix and match your Shrink Ray shenanigans with the Teleporter to find a new perspective!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/e9bedde37c4a718f9656b40f2930ac7f436d92a4.gif[/img]

We're not giving you rifles and pistols. Combat in The Spy Who Shrunk Me is all about utilizing your Shrink Ray. Shrink enemies and drop them down paper shredders or throw them at a wall to lethally eliminate them. Or drop them down a lidded trash can to take them out the pacifist way.


[h1][b]BANANAS[/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/0530059f42cb4a2e02e3ccff4747829a3f5c678c.gif[/img]
Make enemies slip and slide! Enemies who slip on a banana peel are down for the count for a good while, allowing you to slip past undetected.

[h1][b]AIRBAG MINES[/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/0bf72d8d4ae857c14ce1d590dbddcafa9993e348.gif[/img]
Slap one of these bad boys on a wall or floor and watch the enemies fly! Airbag mines give you a chance to get past enemies with ease. 

[h1][b]TELEPORTER RAY[/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/c8fed005a749901ebdf4bd00fb1e5b92e4c3574f.gif[/img]
Reach new heights with the teleporter. Kind of like Blink from your other favorite stealth title, use it to peer above enemies on top of lamps and maneuver yourself on top of tables while shrunk!


[h1][b]MORE TO COME...[/b][/h1]
During Early Access, we aim to add even more wacky gadgets to the game! These include [b]Spytacles[/b] (which let you see enemies through walls!) and the [b]Stopwatch[/b] (which freezes time for a while letting you get past enemies while time stands still!) We'll also take ideas from the community - if you've got a great gadget idea, let us know.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/d374224985bb2649b0962fecd31dc1876ad53d4a.png[/img]

Our VR edition still needs a bit of work! As we've already shipped a very successful and popular VR title [b][url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/591680]Taphouse VR[/url][/b] you know we got what you want in virtual reality:
[list]
[*] Multiple movement options (both teleport and touchpad/thumbstick movement supported)
[*] Accessibility settings like height adjustment, resetting position, toggle for smooth rotation 
[*] Roomscale, sitting and standing play supported from the get-go
[*] Support for major SteamVR headsets
[/list]
We need a bit more time for this, but the ETA is Q1 2019. We have a new technology stack in our game that will support further games down the line with both PC & VR supported, so it's just refining the experience to make sure every bit (including the driving section) works in both formats. We apologize for the delay on this.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33423885/5afba430fae57a1f023b1bf5de7ba50ae83e0844.png[/img]

We will keep you updated on our various social media channels.

We mostly keep our Twitter updated, give it a follow!
[url=https://www.twitter.com/catlandstudios]www.twitter.com/catlandstudios[/url]

We're also going to be dropping even more screenshots and gameplay footage as we go closer to the release! What do you want to see? Let's us know and we'll do our best to spoil you.

Get smooth,
Tomi Toikka
CEO
Catland

Here's a quick status update.

[h1]Release Date[/h1]

Our release date is somewhere in [b]December 2018[/b], we're locking it down and thinking somewhere between 12th and 18th. It all depends on how much content we can cram in that time. Of course things may change so I'll try to keep you posted the best I can.

[h1]What we're working on[/h1]

Our days at the studio has been polishing AI and adding new gadgets. We recently got a new level designer so the game is way more fun to play from the get go - that's why not too many screenshots have been shown since it's all a work in progress!

[h1]New gadgets[/h1]

Two new gadgets in play are the teleporter remote (think Blink or Icarus Dash) and Spytacles which lets you see enemies through walls. We will do our best to get more footage as soon as we can from all these great little things we're working on.

[h1]Taphouse VR: The Spy Who Shilled Me[/h1]
